entries.title: Are the big white parts on a dogwood really petals?
entries.answer: The four big white or pink parts of a flowering dogwood look like petals from far away. In fact, each is a special leaf called a floral bract. They surround a cluster of much smaller flowers. Look toward the middle to see where the actual flowers sit. The big bright bracts help make that cluster visible. Later in the year, the tree can have small red fruits where some of the tiny flowers once grew.
facts: Birds can eat the ripe fruits of flowering dogwood.

questions.text: What is a petal on an ordinary flower?
How can part of a flower become a fruit?
What can an eastern redbud bloom look like before its leaves appear?

entries.title: Are the blue things on an eastern redcedar berries?
entries.answer: At first, the little blue balls on some eastern redcedar branches might look like berries. They are actually seed cones. Their soft scales grow together instead of opening out into a shape like a typical dry pine cone. Birds can eat the cones and carry the seeds to new places. If you look closely at an older twig, you may notice that the tiny green leaves overlap like roof shingles rather than looking like long pine needles.
facts: Despite its name, eastern redcedar is a kind of juniper.

questions.text: How does a dry pine cone release its seeds?
How can an animal carry away a seed?
What shape are the needles on a white pine?

entries.title: Are the little dots on a wild strawberry really seeds?
entries.answer: The dots on the outside of a wild strawberry look like seeds. Each dot is actually a small dry fruit with a seed inside. The soft red part underneath them grows from the base of the flower where its parts were attached. Plenty of fruits look different because they develop in other ways. Close to the ground, a wild strawberry plant can also send out a rooting runner to make new plants at points along their stems.
facts: The surface fruits give a strawberry its bumpy texture.

questions.text: How can one strawberry plant send out stems that make new plants?
How does a tomato form its fruit in a different way?
What does a new plant need to begin growing from a seed?

entries.title: Can two plants with the same leaf color be told apart?
entries.answer: Green leaves can look alike from across a path. Take a closer look and compare the edges and shapes. One leaf may have little teeth, another may have big curved lobes, and a third may have a smooth edge. Look at whether several smaller sections have separate gaps between them or are joined into one flat blade. It's helpful to notice how the leaf joins the plant too, because color and size can change as leaves get older.
facts: People who identify plants often use several clues together.

questions.text: How can a lobe make a shape like the thumb of a mitten?
What is a reliable clue for finding the beginning of one leaf?
How could one breeze help you compare two tree leaves?

entries.title: Can you recognize a white pine by counting needles?
entries.answer: Pine needles are leaves. On an eastern white pine, you can find five fine needles coming out together from the same spot. They form a small needle bundle, so it helps to look at the bases instead of counting every green line on a twig. Other kinds of pine often have fewer needles in each bundle. White pines also grow long, narrow seed cones. The needles stay on through winter, although an individual needle does not stay on forever.
facts: The needles can look bluish green.

questions.text: Which pine usually has three long needles in each bundle?
What do pine cones do for a tree?
How can a tree keep green leaves through winter?

entries.title: Do sunflowers turn to follow the Sun?
entries.answer: A young sunflower may face east in the morning and turn westward by late afternoon. One side of its stem grows faster than the other at different times, bending the plant as it grows. The movement follows a daily rhythm. Once the stem grows more slowly and the flower head matures, the head often stays facing east rather than turning all day. Early sunlight can warm the head, giving it a head start when insects begin visiting after sunrise.
facts: Researchers have found that more pollinating insects can visit warmer, east-facing mature sunflower heads.

questions.text: How can uneven growth bend another kind of plant toward light?
Why do visits from insects matter to flowers?
How can a tall stem hold a flower where it gets more light?

entries.title: Does a live oak ever drop its leaves?
entries.answer: A southern live oak keeps green leaves during winter when it grows in a warm enough place. Still, it sheds older leaves around the time new ones are growing. That is one reason an oak can look green for much of the year even when loose leaves are on the ground. A big tree often spreads broad, low branches that make a wide patch of shade. This oak grows near the Atlantic and Gulf coasts in the southeastern United States.
facts: A southern live oak makes acorns, just as many other oaks do.

questions.text: How can a new oak start inside an acorn?
Do all leaves on an evergreen last for years?
What happens to a sunny spot when a broad tree shades it?

entries.title: Does a red maple have red leaves all year?
entries.answer: A red maple grows green leaves for much of the year. You might spot tiny red flowers in early spring, often well before the leaves spread out. During summer, look along the edges of its leaves. They have little points like the teeth of a saw. In fall, the leaves can turn red, orange, or yellow. That means the name gives you a good clue, but one green leaf in July does not rule out a red maple.
facts: Red maples are native to much of eastern North America.

questions.text: What does a sugar maple leaf look like?
How can a leaf be green in summer and red in fall?
What makes a maple seed spin when it drops?

entries.title: How big can a giant sequoia get?
entries.answer: A giant sequoia builds a trunk wide enough to make people standing beside it look tiny. It is famous for the amount of wood in that trunk. The General Sherman Tree is the largest known living single-stem tree by trunk volume. A few other kinds of trees grow taller, but they do not have trunks with as much wood. Wild giant sequoias grow in groves on the western side of California’s Sierra Nevada. Their seeds are much smaller than the huge trees they can become.
facts: The General Sherman Tree is a giant sequoia in Sequoia National Park.

questions.text: Which related tree often grows much taller?
How do woody cones hold small seeds?
How can water reach leaves so far above the roots?

entries.title: How can a black spruce grow in a bog?
entries.answer: In many northern bogs and other cold wetlands, a skinny black spruce may grow upward where its roots can find a place among the wet peat and moss. It often grows slowly in these conditions. A large tree might have a narrow crown, with short branches and little cones clustered high up. Black spruce also lives in places that are not bogs. Looking at both the tree and what grows around it gives you a fuller picture.
facts: Black spruce can hold some of its seed cones for several years.

questions.text: How can piles of old plant material build up in a bog?
What do the dangling cones of a white spruce look like?
Why do northern forests have so many cone-bearing trees?

entries.title: How can a skunk cabbage flower warm up on a cold day?
entries.answer: A skunk cabbage can open its hooded flower cluster while snow is still on the ground. The cluster uses stored sugars and gives off heat as the plant uses them. It can become warm enough to melt a small space in the snow. The flowers also release an odor that some early flies notice. Later the plant grows broad green leaves. It often lives on wet ground near streams and in swamps.
facts: The odor is one reason the plant is called skunk cabbage.

questions.text: Why do some flowers open before tree leaves appear?
What other plants can live on wet ground?
How can a fly bring pollen to a flower?

entries.title: How can a water lily keep its leaves flat on a pond?
entries.answer: A white water lily grows long flexible stalks from thick stems in the mud. The stalks stretch upward until the roundish leaves spread out on the water. Light reaches the leaf surfaces there, even while the roots stay far below. Each floating leaf often has a slit from its edge partway toward the middle, like a pie with a wedge cut out. Big white flowers can float near the leaves.
facts: The plant can stay attached to the pond bottom while its leaves rest on top.

questions.text: Which plant floats without its roots reaching the mud?
Why are many water plants easier to find in shallow water?
What does a thick stem do below the surface?

entries.title: How can five little green parts still count as one leaf?
entries.answer: On some plants, a compound leaf is divided into a group of smaller pieces called leaflets. Try following the pieces of a Virginia creeper leaf down toward its stem. Five leaflets often join at one place. A single stalk runs from there to the vine. Look for a small bud at the base of the whole leaf where it meets the main stem. The tiny leaflets do not have those buds at their own bases.
facts: A leaf with one undivided blade is called a simple leaf, even if the edges have deep cuts.

questions.text: Which climbing plant usually has five leaflets?
Can a leaf with cuts around the edge still be one flat blade?
What is the little stalk that joins a leaf to a stem?

entries.title: How can moss grow without true roots?
entries.answer: Mosses are small plants that often make soft green mats. Instead of true roots, many have tiny threads that hold the plant in place. Moisture can reach much of a moss plant right through the outside. You may find moss where the ground or a rock stays damp, though some kinds can dry out and start growing again when wet. Moss can spread using spores. These may leave a little case that stands above the green mat.
facts: A moss can grow a spore case at the tip of a slender stalk.

questions.text: How do the true roots of many larger plants carry out different jobs?
Which plants have true roots but still make spores?
What flat or crusty growth on a rock might be a lichen instead of moss?

entries.title: How can one sassafras tree have three leaf shapes?
entries.answer: On a single sassafras tree you might find a plain oval leaf, one shaped like a mitten, and one shaped like a mitten with two thumbs. They really can all belong to the same tree. Each part that looks like a thumb is a leaf lobe. It is a broad piece of the leaf edge. You can find them on some leaves and not on others. Looking at several leaves gives a better clue than picking just one shape.
facts: Many sassafras leaves turn yellow, orange, or red in autumn.

questions.text: What counts as a lobe rather than a separate leaflet?
How is a divided leaf different from a leaf made from separate leaflets?
Why might those leaves change color in autumn?

entries.title: How can Virginia creeper climb a flat wall?
entries.answer: A Virginia creeper grows short curling arms. Each is a climbing tendril. The ends can form little sticky pads where they touch a wall or another solid surface. The pads hold while the stem grows farther upward. You can often spot the vine's leaves even without seeing the pads. Each compound leaf usually has five leaflets spreading out from one point, a little like fingers from a palm.
facts: Virginia creeper can also trail along the ground.

questions.text: Which vine with similar pads often has three pointed leaf lobes?
How do five small parts make up one leaf?
Which vine clings with small roots instead of pads?

entries.title: How can you tell a sugar maple by the gaps in its leaves?
entries.answer: A sugar maple leaf can look like a wide open hand with several pointed lobes. Follow the gap beside a leaf lobe toward the middle. On a sugar maple, that gap often ends with a round curve instead of a sharp corner. The edges usually lack the many fine teeth you find on a red maple. In autumn the leaves can turn yellow, orange, or red, so the shape is often a better clue than the color.
facts: Sugar maple leaves often have five main lobes, with the lowest two noticeably smaller.

questions.text: How can I tell a red maple by its leaves?
How can sap from a sugar maple become syrup?
Why can maple leaves turn bright colors in fall?

entries.title: How do evergreen trees stay green all year?
entries.answer: Evergreen plants keep some green leaves throughout the year. That does not mean that each leaf lasts forever. An evergreen tree can shed older leaves as it grows replacements, rather than dropping most leaves at once. Many pines and spruces have narrow needles with a coating that helps limit water loss. Some other evergreens have wide, flat leaves. The trick is keeping living leaves through winter or a dry season, whatever shape those leaves happen to be.
facts: Some plants with broad, flat leaves are evergreen too.

questions.text: Why do some other trees lose green leaves in fall?
Where does a pine tree grow its seeds?
Which evergreen trees grow especially tall near the Pacific coast?

entries.title: How do leaves help a plant grow?
entries.answer: Leaves give many plants a wide surface to catch sunlight. A green leaf uses light, water and a gas from the air to make sugars. That process is called photosynthesis. The lines you see on many leaves are veins. They bring water in and help move sugars where the plant can use them. Leaves also have tiny openings, often on the lower side. Gases and water vapor can move through those openings even when the leaf looks still.
facts: Some plants have leaves divided into little parts called leaflets.

questions.text: How does the plant turn light and air into sugar?
How can water leave a plant through its leaves?
Why do some leaves turn yellow before they fall?

entries.title: How do seeds get far from the parent plant?
entries.answer: A seed often has a better chance to find space and light if it lands away from its parent. A dandelion makes tiny dry fruits that float in the breeze on little parachutes. A burr can hitch a ride by hooking onto fur or a sock. Other plants hide seeds inside sweet fruit. An animal can eat the fruit, go somewhere else and leave some seeds behind. Some seeds also travel by floating in water or rolling down a slope.
facts: The little parachute on a dandelion helps the fruit carry its seed in the wind.

questions.text: Why can a soft fruit help its seeds travel with an animal?
What happens if one of the seeds lands in a good place to grow?
How can a plant spread nearby without moving seeds?

entries.title: How do white spruce cones hang on the tree?
entries.answer: A white spruce carries its seed cones below the branches like small hanging decorations. They are narrow and have thin scales. A mature cone can come off the tree as a whole piece. Check a balsam fir and you may see its younger cones held up instead of hanging down. The difference is useful because several kinds of northern trees have similar green needles when you see them from far away.
facts: White spruce is an evergreen of northern North America.

questions.text: What happens to the cones that stand up on a balsam fir?
How can scales hide or release seeds?
Which kinds of trees cover many northern forests?

entries.title: How does a bloodroot flower rise from the woods in spring?
entries.answer: A bloodroot flower can begin rising from the ground tucked inside the sides of a folded leaf. The leaf partly wraps around the young flower. When it opens out, the flower often shows a ring of broad white petals and a yellow middle. This happens in the spring, while the light can still reach the woodland floor. The name bloodroot comes from red-orange liquid inside parts of the plant.
facts: Ants can carry its seeds away, just as they do for some other spring plants.

questions.text: Why do so many woodland flowers bloom before the trees are leafy?
How can an ant move a seed away from the plant?
What does a trout lily still have underground after its leaves are gone?

entries.title: How does a dandelion pull off its parachute trick?
entries.answer: The yellow head on a common dandelion is made from many small flowers. Later it can become a white ball filled with what look like tiny parachutes. Each seed parachute is attached to one small dry fruit holding a seed. When a breeze pulls one free, the hairs help it stay in the air longer as it drifts away. A second clue is low to the ground. The plant often has a ring of toothed leaves around its base.
facts: The ring of leaves is called a leaf rosette.

questions.text: Why do some seed hairs work in a breeze while burs stick to fur?
Which plant sends seeds out of a pod on silky threads?
What does a seed need once it lands in a new place?

entries.title: How does a pitcher plant catch insects?
entries.answer: Some pitcher plants make hollow leaves shaped like deep cups. An insect can slip inside and find it hard to climb out. The plant gains nutrients as the captured food breaks down. In a purple pitcher plant, rain can collect in the leaf and tiny living things may help break down the material inside. This can help a plant in a wet place where its roots cannot find a large supply of certain nutrients. The pitcher is a special kind of leaf.
facts: Some pitcher plants have leaves that collect rainwater.

questions.text: Which plant can snap a leaf shut?
How does a leaf usually help a plant make sugar?
What normal job do roots perform in most plants?

entries.title: How does a plant send sugar to its roots?
entries.answer: A leaf might make more sugar than it needs right away. The plant can send some of that sugar to other places through a tissue called phloem. A growing root or fruit might use the sugar, or a plant part might store it. The direction depends on where sugars are ready to move and where they are needed. Later, sugar released from a storage part can travel to a new shoot, even before that shoot has many leaves.
facts: Growing roots and fruits can receive sugars through phloem.

questions.text: Where does most of the sugar in a leafy plant come from?
Which tissue carries water up from the roots?
Which plant parts often receive sugars as they grow?

entries.title: How does a plant spread by underground stems?
entries.answer: A rhizome is a stem that grows sideways, often just below the ground. Roots can grow down from it. New leafy shoots can grow up at points along the stem. That is one way irises fill more space over time. The old and new shoots can stay connected through the rhizome even when only their tops are visible. A rhizome can also store food, giving a new shoot a supply before it grows enough leaves to make its own.
facts: The part of a ginger plant sold as “ginger root” is actually a rhizome.

questions.text: What kind of stem spreads across the top of the ground?
Which swollen stem can store food and sprout from eyes?
What makes a plant part a stem even when it is underground?

entries.title: How does a root know which way is down?
entries.answer: A root does not need to see the ground to grow down into it. Certain cells near many root tips can detect the direction of gravity. Signals from those cells affect how much parts of the root grow. If a seed is turned sideways, a new root can soon curve downward. Stems often respond by bending upward. The growth pattern is called gravitropism. It helps a seed get some roots into the ground and some shoots toward open space where leaves can catch light.
facts: Shoots and many roots can respond in opposite directions to gravity.

questions.text: How can light make a shoot bend even while gravity pulls on it?
What new parts start to grow when a seed sprouts?
How does growing down give a root a better chance to find water?

entries.title: How does a saguaro cactus keep water inside?
entries.answer: Look at a saguaro and you can see long folds down its green stem. They let the stem swell when the cactus takes in water and draw in as it uses that stored water. Roots that spread out near the surface can pick up some water after a rain. The stem handles jobs that leaves do in many other plants, including making food with the help of sunlight.
facts: A saguaro grows in the Sonoran Desert, in parts of the southwestern United States and Mexico.

questions.text: Why can a desert wash fill during a storm?
What do roots do in other plants?
How does sunlight help a plant make food?

entries.title: How does a saguaro cactus save water?
entries.answer: A saguaro has a tall, green stem with folds along its sides. It can store water in that stem when rain is available. As more water enters, the folds unfold some, so the stem can get thicker. Many roots stretch sideways just below the surface, where some rain can quickly reach them. A slow-growing saguaro can live through dry stretches using water already inside. Its sharp spines are different from the wide, thin leaves you might see on a garden plant.
facts: Saguaros grow naturally in the Sonoran Desert and nearby areas.

questions.text: How can spreading roots help soak up water after a rain?
What is one way water usually leaves a plant?
What jobs can a green stem do in a cactus that has no broad leaves?

entries.title: How does a seed wake up and grow?
entries.answer: A dry seed can hold a tiny plant and its food supply for a long time. When conditions fit what that kind of plant needs, the seed takes in water and swells. A little root often breaks through the seed coat first. A shoot can then grow in another direction and reach the light. Early on, the young plant uses food stored in the seed. After green leaves open, the plant can make more of its own sugar.
facts: For many kinds of seeds, the root begins growing before the shoot.

questions.text: What is hidden inside a seed before it sprouts?
How does a new root keep the seedling supplied with water?
What changes once a young plant has green leaves?

entries.title: How does a strawberry plant make a runner?
entries.answer: A strawberry plant can stretch a long, thin stem across the soil. The stem is called a runner. At places along it, a little copy of the plant can grow leaves and reach down with new roots. At first the tiny plant is joined to the older one. Once its roots and leaves can do enough work, it can survive on its own. This lets one strawberry plant make several nearby plants even in a season when it makes few seeds.
facts: A stem that runs along the ground to make new plants can also be called a stolon.

questions.text: Which sideways-growing stems are usually found underground?
What other ways can plants spread to new places?
What can a new strawberry plant do after it grows its own roots?

entries.title: How does a trumpet vine hang on while it climbs?
entries.answer: A trumpet vine can hold onto rough bark or another solid surface with little roots growing out of the stem. The small roots reach into rough spots and help support the vine as it grows. They are not the same as the large underground roots that supply much of its water. The plant often has long orange or red flowers. Their narrow bases can hold nectar that a hummingbird can reach.
facts: Each small aboveground root helps hold the vine in place.

questions.text: Which vine grips a surface with sticky pads at the ends of tendrils?
How can a hummingbird hang in the air in front of a flower?
What jobs do ordinary underground roots do?

entries.title: How does a Venus flytrap catch a fly?
entries.answer: A Venus flytrap has hinged leaves with tiny hairs on their inside surfaces. When a small insect moves around and brushes the right hairs within a short time, a leaf can snap closed. The plant can get helpful nutrients from the trapped animal. It lives in places where some nutrients are hard to get from the ground. Its green parts still use sunlight to make sugars, as the leaves of other green plants do. Catching animals helps the plant meet a different need.
facts: Wild Venus flytraps are native to a small part of North and South Carolina.

questions.text: What different shape can a plant use to trap insects?
Where does a flytrap get much of the energy it uses?
How do most plants get minerals from soil?

entries.title: How does water reach the top of a tree?
entries.answer: When water leaves a tree’s leaves as vapor, it helps pull more water upward. Water molecules tend to cling to one another. This lets the pull travel down columns of water inside tiny tubes. The tubes are part of a water-carrying tissue called xylem. Water from the soil enters the roots and helps refill those columns. The whole path can reach from the fine tips of roots to leaves at the very top of a tree.
facts: Water can travel through a path of connected xylem cells.

questions.text: How does water vapor leave the leaf?
Which tissue carries sugars from leaves to growing parts?
How wide can the trunk of a giant tree grow?

entries.title: How does white clover creep across a lawn?
entries.answer: A stem of white clover can lie flat on top of the soil. As it grows longer, roots can form where parts of the stem touch the ground. New leaves and flower stalks rise at points along it. A stem that spreads this way is a rooting runner. The flower heads can be white or slightly pink, while the low green leaves often have three leaflets. You may see pale bands on the little green leaflets.
facts: The creeping stem above the ground is called a stolon.

questions.text: Which plant also spreads by making new roots on long runners?
Which kind of clover usually has a pink flower head?
How can three green parts all belong to one leaf?

entries.title: How does witch hazel shoot some of its seeds away?
entries.answer: On common witch hazel, a ripe seed case can dry and bend out of shape. The squeezing sides can suddenly force a seed out, a little like a wet soap bar slipping from a tight hand. The seed may land away from the parent shrub instead of dropping beside it. The same plant also makes yellow flowers with narrow, twisted petals. Many appear in fall, after most other woodland shrubs have finished blooming.
facts: It is possible to see flowers and older seed cases on the same plant.

questions.text: Which orange-flowered plant also throws seeds from a ripe pod?
What other ways move seeds away from their parents?
Which small plant also makes flowers late in the year?

entries.title: How plants make their own food
entries.answer: A green plant uses sunlight, water, and a gas called carbon dioxide to make sugar. This is photosynthesis. In many plants most of the work happens in the leaves. A green material called chlorophyll helps catch energy from light. With that energy, the plant makes sugars it can use to grow or store for later. During this process the plant also gives off oxygen. The water usually comes from the soil, and the carbon dioxide enters the plant from the air.
facts: Chlorophyll helps give many leaves their green color.
Many algae use light to make sugars too.

questions.text: How do tiny algae help a reef coral get food?
What happens to the Sun’s energy when a plant makes sugar?
How can a young plant start growing before it has leaves?

entries.title: How pollen travels from flower to flower
entries.answer: Flowers can make tiny grains called pollen. For many flowers to make seeds, pollen must reach a part of a flower that can receive it. Moving pollen there is called pollination. A bee that visits a flower for food can pick up pollen on its body. On the next flower, some grains can rub off. Some plants use wind to move pollen instead. Plants often need a match between the kind of pollen and the kind of flower, so pollen landing anywhere is only one step in making seeds.
facts: Wind can carry pollen from some kinds of plants.
Bees are not the only animals that can carry pollen.

questions.text: What can grow after a flower makes a seed?
Can a bat visit flowers and carry pollen?
How does the plant get the energy it needs to grow flowers?

entries.title: How seeds start new plants
entries.answer: A seed holds the beginnings of a new plant. A coat helps protect the tiny plant inside. Many seeds also hold food that the young plant can use before it has leaves. With the right conditions, a seed can start to grow. Some seeds are carried by the wind. Others hitch a ride on an animal’s fur or travel inside a fruit that an animal eats. When a seed ends up far from its parent, the new plant may get more light or space to grow.
facts: Some seeds can travel by water.
Germination is the beginning of a seed’s growth.

questions.text: How can pollen help a flowering plant make seeds?
How does a young plant feed itself once its leaves grow?
How does rainwater get into the ground around roots?

entries.title: Is a red clover head one big flower or many small ones?
entries.answer: A red clover's pink ball looks like one flower until you look closely. It is a flower head made of small flowers, each shaped a little like a pea flower. A bee can visit several during one stop on the plant. Look at the leaves too. The parts that look like three leaves are three leaflets on a shared stem, together making one compound leaf. Each may show a pale mark shaped a little like an arrow.
facts: Red clover flowers usually look pink or purplish rather than bright red.

questions.text: Which clover spreads low along the ground?
What makes several leaflets part of one leaf?
How can bumblebees reach pollen in some other flowers?

entries.title: What are pine cones for?
entries.answer: Pine trees make cones as part of making seeds. Small pollen cones release pollen into the air. A larger seed cone has scales, the stiff plates you can see on a pine cone. Seeds grow where they are protected by those scales. In some species, a cone opens when it dries, and the seeds can fall or blow away. A pine tree does not make a fruit around its seeds, which is one way it differs from a tomato plant.
facts: A pine has small pollen cones as well as larger seed cones.

questions.text: How does pollen travel even when a plant has no petals?
How can a small cone come from a gigantic tree?
How do flowering plants cover their seeds differently?

entries.title: What are the eyes on a potato?
entries.answer: The eyes on a potato are places where buds can grow. Each bud can start a shoot if the potato has suitable conditions. A potato is a tuber, a thick storage part that develops on an underground stem. It holds food the plant made earlier. Because it is a stem part, a potato can make new shoots at several points. The thick part of a sweet potato may look similar from the outside, but it is a storage root.
facts: A sweet potato and a regular potato store food in different parts of the plant.

questions.text: What does a true root do?
How does a tulip store food in a different way?
How else can a stem grow underground?

entries.title: What are the green specks floating on a quiet pond?
entries.answer: In a quiet pond, a thin green mat might break apart into tiny pieces as water moves. If it is common duckweed, each little green piece belongs to a small floating plant. Look from close enough to see its slender root hanging in the water. A new green piece can grow from the edge and break away. Given enough light and space, many plants can cover part of the water almost like paint.
facts: Each small floating plant usually has one root pointing down.

questions.text: Which pond plant has much larger flat leaves?
Why are so many kinds of plant found near a pond's edge?
What different jobs can plant roots do?

entries.title: What can grow from a white oak acorn?
entries.answer: A white oak grows acorns, the hard nuts found under the tree. Much of an acorn gives food and protection to its seed while it waits. Some animals eat acorns right away. Squirrels and jays can also carry them to save for later. An acorn that stays hidden in damp ground may send down a root and grow into a young oak. The acorn’s food can help that plant before it has a crown of leaves to catch much light.
facts: White oak acorns usually begin sending out a root soon after they fall if conditions are suitable.

questions.text: How can animals carry seeds a long way from a tree?
Which part may begin growing first when a seed sprouts?
How does wind move a seed from a different kind of tree?

entries.title: What can the underside of a magnolia leaf show?
entries.answer: A southern magnolia often has thick leaves that look shiny and dark green from above. Many have a fuzzy brown patch across the underneath side. If you find a fallen leaf, try turning it over to compare the surfaces. Some trees have less fuzz than others. In warm months, the branches may carry big white flowers. Later a bumpy, cone-shaped fruit can open and expose bright red seeds.
facts: Southern magnolia is a leafy evergreen and can keep leaves through the winter.

questions.text: Which magnolia relative has a tulip-shaped flower?
How can a tree with broad leaves stay green in winter?
How can a firm, bumpy plant part count as a fruit?

entries.title: What can you spot on a common blue violet before it flowers?
entries.answer: In a lawn or at a shady woodland edge, you may see small leaves with a dip at the wide end and a point at the narrow end. That outline looks like a green heart. On a common blue violet, the leaves rise from near the ground, each on its own leaf stem. In spring, the plant often makes blue-violet flowers. Some plants have pale flowers instead. The outline of the leaf is a clue even when no petals are showing.
facts: Some common blue violets also make small closed flowers that can produce seed.

questions.text: How does a leaf attach to the main shoot of a plant?
Why do many low flowers bloom in spring?
Which tree has heart-shaped leaves too?

entries.title: What do ants carry away from a white trillium?
entries.answer: A great white trillium often has one broad white flower above three green leaf-like parts. The flower has three petals, and old white petals sometimes turn pink. When seeds ripen, an ant can find a small food-rich piece attached to one. The ant may carry away the whole seed to reach that food. After the food part is removed, the seed can still be left somewhere new.
facts: Trillium flowers commonly open early in spring woodland.

questions.text: Why would an ant carry a seed instead of eating the whole thing?
What is the advantage of opening before the trees get leafy?
Which parts of a flower are petals?

entries.title: What do plant roots do?
entries.answer: A plant’s roots reach into soil or another place where the plant grows. They help hold the plant steady when wind pushes on the leaves. Many roots also soak up water and minerals. The plant moves those supplies to other parts, including new shoots. A carrot has a thick main root that stores food. Grass often has a spreading bunch of thinner roots. A plant can have important parts below the ground even when you only see leaves above it.
facts: Many roots have tiny root hairs that help take in water.

questions.text: Where does water go after it enters the roots?
What living partners can help roots get minerals?
Is an underground potato a root or a stem?

entries.title: What does a leaf stem do besides hold up a leaf?
entries.answer: A leaf stem joins the wide part of many leaves to a plant's main stem. Botanists call this leaf stalk a petiole. Inside are tiny tubes that connect with the tubes in the main stem and the leaf. Water can move toward the leaf, and sugars can leave it for other parts of the plant. The stalk also holds the flat part of the leaf where it may get enough light.
facts: Not every leaf has a stalk. Some attach right against the main stem.

questions.text: How does water get from roots up to leaves?
How can a single leaf stalk support several leaflets?
Why can a flattened leaf stalk make an aspen leaf move?

entries.title: What floats away when a milkweed pod opens?
entries.answer: A common milkweed pod is firm and green when it is young. As it dries, the pod can split along one side. Inside are rows of flat seeds. Each seed is attached to a tuft of fine, silky threads. The threads can spread in the air like a tiny parachute and carry the seed away from the old plant. Before pods develop, the plant makes round groups of small fragrant flowers.
facts: Monarch caterpillars can feed on milkweed leaves.

questions.text: What are other ways plants move their seeds away?
Why do many monarch butterflies travel south in fall?
Which other milkweed has orange flower clusters?

entries.title: What happens to an upright balsam fir cone when its seeds ripen?
entries.answer: Many cone-bearing trees hang their seed cones below branches. Balsam fir cones sit above the branches. When a ripe fir cone releases its seeds, its scales can break apart while it is still standing there. That is why you may find the main stalk still attached instead of finding a complete fir cone on the ground. Check the needles of a nearby twig too. The underside has two pale stripes.
facts: Balsam fir is an evergreen native to eastern North America.

questions.text: Which northern tree holds cones that hang down?
What parts of a cone protect its seeds?
What does a forest of many firs and spruces look like?

entries.title: What holds Boston ivy to a brick wall?
entries.answer: Look for little pads at the ends of the thin branches coming from a Boston ivy climbing tendril. The pads can stick to rough surfaces. They help the vine hold itself high enough to reach more light. A young leaf can look different from an older one, but many mature leaves have three pointed parts. The leaves can turn deep red before dropping in autumn, leaving stems and some pads behind.
facts: Boston ivy is a relative of grapes, not a true ivy.

questions.text: Which climbing grape relative usually has five leaflets?
What other plant uses roots to hold onto objects?
What changes can make ivy leaves turn red?

entries.title: What is a black walnut hiding inside its green husk?
entries.answer: The round green things on a black walnut branch may look a little like small balls. Each one holds a very hard shell around a seed. The green cover is called a husk. As the fruit ages, the husk gets softer and can turn dark. It contains a strong stain that can color hands and clothes. Long leaves on the same tree look like rows of small leaves, but the pieces belong to one big compound leaf.
facts: The combined outer husk and hard shell protect the seed as it grows.

questions.text: Which nut tree has bark that hangs in long strips?
How can I tell a whole walnut leaf from one of its pieces?
Why might a squirrel carry a nut away instead of eating it now?

entries.title: What is hidden inside a tulip bulb?
entries.answer: A tulip bulb packs together a short stem, a new bud and thick layers that hold food. Most of this rests underground when the plant has no green top. When conditions are right, a shoot can rise and use that stored food. Roots can grow from the small hard base. An onion is another kind of bulb. Its fleshy rings are easier to see than the tightly packed layers of a tulip bulb, but their storage job is much the same.
facts: An onion’s thick layers are mostly storage leaves.

questions.text: How is a potato different from a layered bulb?
How does a plant refill its food supply once leaves open?
What kind of underground stem can grow sideways?

entries.title: What is hidden underneath a jack-in-the-pulpit's green hood?
entries.answer: A jack-in-the-pulpit grows a green or striped hood that curls over a narrow standing spike. The hood is a large leaf-like part, a kind of floral bract. Look lower on the spike and the actual flowers are tiny and close together. The hood surrounds them like the roof of a little booth. After flowering, some plants grow a tight cluster of red fruits instead. This plant often grows in moist woods and shady places.
facts: Each large leaf is usually divided into three leaflets.

questions.text: Which tree also has showy parts around much smaller flowers?
How can new fruit grow from parts of a flower?
How can the three parts on a stem be parts of one leaf?

entries.title: What is inside a black-eyed Susan's dark eye?
entries.answer: The dark center on a black-eyed Susan looks like one round button, but a close look can show many little flowers. The tiny ones make up a raised disk. Yellow petal-like parts spread out around the edge, making the whole flower head easy to notice. The stems and leaves often feel rough because they have short hairs. This plant can grow in open places and may bloom for part of summer and fall.
facts: The name hirta refers to the plant's hairy surfaces.

questions.text: How does another plant build a whole head out of small flowers?
What can happen when an insect visits those flowers?
What other plants can grow in a sunny open prairie?

entries.title: What is inside a flower?
entries.answer: Colorful petals are the most obvious parts of many flowers. Look closer and you may see small structures that make pollen or collect it. In many flowers, the pollen makers are called stamens. A sticky surface called a stigma can catch grains of pollen. Below it, part of the flower can grow into a fruit with seeds. Some kinds of flowers have all these parts together. Other kinds put pollen-making and seed-making parts in different flowers.
facts: The stamens are the pollen-making parts of many flowers.

questions.text: How does pollen get from one flower to another?
What happens to a flower’s ovary as a fruit grows?
How does a seed start to grow by itself?

entries.title: What is the prickly middle of a coneflower made of?
entries.answer: A purple coneflower seems to have a big ring of petals around one spiky middle. The middle is actually made of lots of tiny flowers packed close together. Their pointed parts can make the center look prickly. The purple shapes around the edge are parts of other flowers in the same flower head. Later the head dries, but the tiny center flowers can leave seeds behind. Birds sometimes visit these dry heads.
facts: Purple coneflowers belong to the same plant family as daisies.

questions.text: Which yellow flower also has a center made of tiny flowers?
Why do goldfinches come looking for seeds?
What parts can I find in a bigger, single flower?

entries.title: What lives around the flower clusters on a New Jersey tea shrub?
entries.answer: New Jersey tea is a small native shrub that can grow along a forest edge or in an open meadow. In early summer, the ends of many branches carry bunches of tiny white flowers. Bees and other insects can stop to drink nectar at them. The leaves can also be eaten by caterpillars of some butterflies. Look from a short distance and one shrub can seem like a little neighborhood with visitors working in several parts.
facts: The shrub grows in central and eastern North America.

questions.text: How can an area provide flowers for different visitors?
What other plant has many little flower heads packed together?
What makes a forest edge different from a place deep in the woods?

entries.title: What makes a leaf lobe different from a leaflet?
entries.answer: A leaf lobe is an outward piece along the edge of a leaf that is still connected to the leaf blade. Run your eyes around a fallen maple leaf. You can see the big pointed parts on the edge, but the green tissue still joins them. A leaflet is usually separate from the other leaflets, even though they share one leaf stalk. Some leaves have deep cuts that make the difference tricky at first.
facts: A mitten-shaped sassafras leaf has a round lobe like a thumb.

questions.text: Can a single tree have leaves with different numbers of lobes?
How do I tell one compound leaf from a set of small leaves?
What clues are on the edge of a red maple leaf?

entries.title: What makes a purple passionflower look like a clock face?
entries.answer: A purple passionflower can look as if somebody placed a ring of thin threads on top of a wide flower. The threads spread out from the middle over the outer parts, making rings of purple and white. The upright parts in the middle are involved in making and receiving pollen. The plant is a vine, and it can hang onto a nearby support with curling tendrils. Some flowers are followed by round or egg-shaped fruits.
facts: Another common name for this species is maypop.

questions.text: Which parts of a flower can make or receive pollen?
How does a different vine climb with tendrils?
How does a fruit start to grow after flowering?

entries.title: What makes a Queen Anne's lace flower head look like lace?
entries.answer: A head of Queen Anne's lace can look flat from the side and lacy when you look down at it. Many little white flowers sit on groups of stalks that spread like the ribs of an umbrella. After flowering, these stalks may bend inward to make a cup that people compare with a bird's nest. The plant is a wild carrot relative, but looking like a carrot is never enough to tell whether a wild plant can be eaten.
facts: An umbrella-shaped group of flower stalks is called an umbel.

questions.text: What can I find in one flower when it is not packed in a group?
How does a clover arrange small flowers in a different shape?
What can happen when a plant spreads far from its original range?

entries.title: What makes a shagbark hickory look scruffy?
entries.answer: Look at an older shagbark hickory trunk and you may see thick strips of gray outer bark peeling away from it. The ends of the strips often stick out, while parts of the strips remain attached. The trunk can look like it is covered in loose boards. In summer, each compound leaf has several smaller pieces. It also makes nuts that grow inside thick husks, which split as the nuts ripen.
facts: Young shagbark hickories have smoother bark than old ones.

questions.text: How is thin birch bark different from thick hickory bark?
When do several small pieces together count as one leaf?
What does a black walnut look like before its husk comes off?

entries.title: What shape is a ginkgo leaf?
entries.answer: A ginkgo leaf spreads out like a little fan on a long handle. Lines of tiny tubes start near the handle and fork again and again as they reach the wide edge. Some leaves have a dip in the middle of that edge, while others have almost no dip. The leaves can all turn a bright yellow before dropping. Ginkgo is also called a maidenhair tree because its leaves remind people of the small fans on maidenhair ferns.
facts: A ginkgo tree makes seeds but does not make flowers.

questions.text: Why do some maidenhair fern leaves look like small fans?
Where do yellow fall colors come from?
What do the lines on the surface of a leaf carry?

entries.title: What sticks out between the scales of a Douglas-fir cone?
entries.answer: A Douglas-fir cone has thin parts sticking out between its overlapping scales. Each of these parts has three points. The middle one is long and thin, so it can look a bit like a tiny tail between two feet. The shape is an easy clue if you find a fallen cone. Douglas-firs grow in western North America, and coastal trees and trees in the Rocky Mountains can look different from each other.
facts: Douglas-fir is not a member of the same genus as balsam fir.

questions.text: Where do balsam fir cones point while they grow?
What protects the seeds between the pieces of a cone?
What makes a rain forest cool and wet instead of hot?

entries.title: Where do the blue chicory flowers go in the afternoon?
entries.answer: You can see bright blue chicory flowers on some roadsides in the morning. A flower head may close later in the day, so the same plant can look much plainer in the afternoon. Look along its stiff, branching stems. The blue heads do not grow as one big bunch at the top. You can often see a few set apart at different places along the stems.
facts: Each blue head is made of many strap-shaped tiny flowers.

questions.text: Which low lawn plant also makes a flower head from many smaller parts?
Why are some flowers open in the morning and others later?
What does the yellow center of an aster contain?

entries.title: Where do the lines in a leaf go?
entries.answer: A leaf can look like a tiny road map if you hold it where light shines through. The big lines are veins, with finer lines leading away from them. Tiny tubes within the veins move water and other materials through the leaf. Veins also help support the thin green surface. A grass leaf often has long veins running in almost the same direction. In many broad leaves, the small veins branch into a web.
facts: Many leaves have one broad leaf vein running down the middle.

questions.text: What shape do the branching veins make on a ginkgo leaf?
How can water reach the veins in a very high leaf?
How does sugar get out of a leaf and travel to a root?

entries.title: Which little spring flower looks like upside-down pants?
entries.answer: A row of white Dutchman's breeches flowers may look like tiny pants hung by their waists. Two pointed parts stick upward from each hanging flower. These spurs hold nectar. The leaves are divided into many narrow pieces and sit lower than the curved flower stem. In the spring woods, the plant can be easy to see for a short time. After blooming, its aboveground growth can disappear by summer.
facts: Ants help spread the plant’s seeds.

questions.text: Which spring flower also has nectar tucked away in spurs?
Why does more sunlight reach the ground in spring?
What can lead an ant to carry an entire seed somewhere new?

entries.title: Which northern tree drops whole bunches of soft needles?
entries.answer: For part of summer, a tamarack twig carries lots of soft needles in little bunches. If you look at a new shoot, you can also see single needles along it. In autumn, the green needles turn gold before dropping. In winter the branches can look bare except for little cones. This is different from a nearby black spruce, which keeps green needles. Tamarack grows in much of northern North America, including many peatlands.
facts: Tamarack is also called American larch.

questions.text: Which tree in a northern bog keeps its needles through winter?
Which other tree makes cones but sheds its needles?
How does wet, partly decayed plant material build up in a bog?

entries.title: Which orange wildflower is also a milkweed?
entries.answer: A patch of butterfly weed can look like little orange umbrellas standing over the grass. Each umbrella is a cluster of small flowers. Butterflies and bees can visit to drink nectar. Even though its flowers are a different color from common milkweed's, this plant is also a milkweed. Monarch caterpillars can eat its leaves. Butterfly weed often grows in sunny fields and dry, open places. Its young shoots can come back from the roots in another year.
facts: Unlike many milkweeds, butterfly weed usually has clear sap.

questions.text: What does a common milkweed pod look like inside?
How can a flower visitor move pollen?
How can a garden feed insects at more than one time of year?

entries.title: Which pine grows in old fields in the southeastern U.S.?
entries.answer: A loblolly pine can grow in sunny places where farm fields or other open ground used to be. Seeds from nearby trees can find enough light there to start new trees. Look along the branches for a needle bundle with three long needles. The lower branches often disappear as the tree grows taller. A group of old loblollies can have tall bare trunks with most of the green parts high above your head.
facts: Loblolly pine is native to the southeastern United States.

questions.text: How many needles usually grow together on a white pine?
How can trees eventually grow in an old field?
Where do pine seeds form?

entries.title: Which wetland plant can have a flower as wide as a dinner plate?
entries.answer: A swamp rose mallow can have flowers several inches across. The petals may be pale with a dark red center, or pink with darker marks. Look toward the middle and you will often see a long piece projecting out from the flower. Many of the little parts that make pollen are arranged around it. Although the flowers look like tropical hibiscus, the plant grows naturally in parts of eastern North America, often on wet ground.
facts: Old flowers may leave a dry seed pod behind.

questions.text: Which other tall flower grows near wet places?
What else might grow near a mallow in a marsh?
What is the name for a part that makes pollen?

entries.title: Why are coast redwoods famous?
entries.answer: Coast redwoods are the tallest living trees known. They grow naturally along a narrow stretch of the Pacific coast in California and a small part of Oregon. Winter rain and summer fog help keep their forests moist. A redwood may rise far above the plants at its foot, yet its cones are fairly small. A redwood’s height tells you one thing about its size. A giant sequoia’s wider trunk often contains more wood even when the giant sequoia is shorter.
facts: Coast redwood and giant sequoia are two different kinds of trees.

questions.text: Why does “largest tree” sometimes refer to a different tree?
What helps water travel all the way up a redwood?
What does it mean for a tree to be evergreen?

entries.title: Why can American holly stay green in winter?
entries.answer: An American holly keeps its tough, waxy leaves through cold weather instead of dropping them all in autumn. The leaves often have pointed teeth along the edge. Some trees also carry bright red fruits that stand out against their green foliage. These fruits grow on trees with seed-making flowers. A bird may carry seeds to new ground after eating the fruit, where the seeds have a chance to grow.
facts: American holly is native to parts of eastern and central North America.

questions.text: Which kind of oak holds green leaves into winter?
How can a bird move plant seeds?
How do leaves help a plant when there is enough light?

entries.title: Why can redbud branches turn pink before spring leaves open?
entries.answer: An eastern redbud can look like a bare tree covered with tiny pink beads near the start of spring. Those are flowers opening along the branches before the leaves spread. Some flowers grow straight from older parts of the tree. Later, the wide leaves look rather like small green hearts. Some flowers also turn into long, thin seed pods. You can sometimes see the old pods on the branches in winter.
facts: Eastern redbuds belong to the same large plant family as peas.

questions.text: Where are the tiny flowers on a showy dogwood?
How can a fruit form after a flower is pollinated?
Why do many small woodland flowers open early too?

entries.title: Why can the top of a blazing star flower stalk bloom first?
entries.answer: A dense blazing star carries rows of small purple flower heads along a straight tall stem. In many plants, the heads at the top start to open earlier than the ones below. For a time, the stem can have open fuzzy flowers high up and tight buds lower down. It gives visiting insects different parts of the stem to check over time. You may find this plant growing in a moist open meadow.
facts: Blazing stars are related to asters and other members of the daisy family.

questions.text: What does another North American aster's flower head look like?
Why might flowers be open at different times?
What kinds of grasses and flowers live in wet open sites?

entries.title: Why do aspen leaves shake in a small breeze?
entries.answer: Hold a sheet of paper by one edge and it can wobble in a breeze. The roundish leaves of a quaking aspen wobble especially easily because each sits on a leaf stem that is flattened from side to side. Even a small breeze can twist the stem and shake the leaf. The moving leaves may flash green and pale when the light hits them from different angles. In fall, many aspen leaves turn yellow.
facts: A quaking aspen is a kind of poplar.

questions.text: What does a leaf stem do besides hold up a leaf?
Why do aspen leaves turn yellow in fall?
Which kind of poplar sends soft white fluff into the air?

entries.title: Why do black willows often grow beside water?
entries.answer: A black willow can grow on wet ground along rivers, lakes, and other low places. Like many willows, it makes very small seeds with light hairs that help them float away. A bare patch of damp ground gives a seed a good place to start. The tree is also useful to notice by its thin, pointed leaves. Its leaves do not look much like the broad green leaves of many other riverside trees.
facts: Black willow is native to much of the eastern United States.

questions.text: Which other riverside tree sends seeds off with white fluff?
How can trees by a stream change the water's edge?
What makes a weeping willow look different?

entries.title: Why do burdock burs follow you home on your socks?
entries.answer: A dry burdock head has lots of tiny curved tips on its outside. Those tips can catch threads in a sock or grab hairs in an animal's coat. A whole head may come off the plant and travel far from the spot where it grew. The part that sticks is a cluster around a group of dry fruits. Each fruit can carry a seed. A head with hooks is called a hooked bur.
facts: The hooks grip much better than a smooth, round seed would.

questions.text: How is traveling on fur different from flying on hairs?
How do tiny hooks help two strips of a fastener stick?
What are other ways plant seeds travel?

entries.title: Why do cattails have brown heads that turn fluffy?
entries.answer: A cattail’s tall brown head holds many tiny fruits that carry seeds. When the head breaks apart, they can drift off with a tuft of fine hairs. The hairs help the pieces catch air so wind can move them away from the parent plant. If a seed reaches wet ground with the right conditions, it can sprout. Cattails can also grow new shoots from spreading stems below the ground.
facts: A stand of cattails can spread both by sending seeds away and by growing new shoots close by.

questions.text: What kinds of soft-stemmed plants grow in a marsh?
How else can plants send their seeds away?
What is a stem that grows sideways under the ground?

entries.title: Why do leaves change color in fall?
entries.answer: A summer maple leaf looks green because it has a lot of a substance called chlorophyll. In fall, as days get shorter, the leaf makes less chlorophyll and the green color fades. Other colors that were harder to see can now show through. They include some yellow and orange colors. Some leaves make additional red or purple coloring in fall. Different kinds of trees can turn different colors, and light and temperature can help change how bright the colors look.
facts: Yellow or orange colors can already be present before a green leaf changes color.

questions.text: What is chlorophyll helping a green leaf do in summer?
How do some trees stay green all winter?
How can a tree move some sugars away from a leaf?

entries.title: Why do little maple “helicopters” spin?
entries.answer: Many maples have dry fruits with a thin wing around or beside a pocket holding a seed. When a fruit falls, the wing can make it turn in the air. The turning slows its trip to the ground. A breeze gets more time to push it sideways, so the seed may land farther from the parent tree. Two fruits often start joined in a pair before they separate. The little “helicopter” you find already carries everything enclosed with that seed.
facts: A winged maple fruit is called a samara.

questions.text: How can wings, hooks or juicy fruits move seeds in different ways?
What part of a sugar maple do people collect for syrup?
How can a seed grow after it settles on the ground?

entries.title: Why do maidenhair fern leaves look like little fans?
entries.answer: A northern maidenhair fern lifts its greenery on thin dark stems. Look from above and you may see the stems spread sideways instead of sitting in one straight line. Along them are many small flat pieces that can look like open fans. These pieces are parts of a fern leaf, which is called a fern frond. A maidenhair fern does not make flowers. It grows little groups of spores on the edges of some of those fans.
facts: A spore is tiny, much smaller than an acorn or bean seed.

questions.text: Where do other kinds of fern carry their spores?
Which tree also has leaves shaped like fans?
How can we tell whether small parts belong to one leaf?

entries.title: Why do plants have stems?
entries.answer: A stem holds plant parts in places where they can do their jobs. A tall stem can lift leaves toward the light. It can also raise flowers where insects or wind can reach them. Inside many stems, tiny passageways carry water and sugars. Stems can be soft, like the stem of a bean plant, or hard and woody, like a tree trunk. Some run sideways instead of growing up. Others are hidden underground and store food.
facts: A tree trunk is a type of stem.

questions.text: Where does most of a plant’s water enter?
Which part of the stem carries water up?
What happens when a stem grows sideways across the ground?

entries.title: Why do plants release water vapor?
entries.answer: Water from damp cells inside a leaf can turn into vapor. That vapor escapes through small openings called stomata. The process is called transpiration. Humid air already holds a lot of water vapor, so the loss is often slower in humid air than in dry air. A steady loss of water through leaves helps move more water up through the plant. If water is scarce, closing the openings can slow the loss and help the plant hold on to water.
facts: Plants can change how wide their stomata open.

questions.text: How does water loss near the top of a plant help pull water upward?
Where else does water vapor come from?
How does a plant replace the water it loses?

entries.title: Why do ripe jewelweed pods pop open?
entries.answer: A spotted jewelweed makes orange flowers with darker spots. Later, it grows narrow green seed pods. In a ripe pod the pieces of the wall are ready to curl up. When one lets go, the wall comes apart quickly and sends seeds away from the plant. That movement gave jewelweed a second name, touch-me-not. The pods on a nearby plant may still be young enough to stay tightly shut.
facts: Some jewelweed grows in damp places near a stream or forest edge.

questions.text: Which shrub can send seeds flying from hard little cases?
How can seeds travel without help from wind or animals?
What other kinds of plant can grow by a stream?

entries.title: Why do shoots sometimes bend toward a window?
entries.answer: A young stem beside a window can bend as it grows. The side away from the strongest light can stretch more than the lit side. With one side getting longer, the whole stem curves toward the window. Bending as it grows can put its leaves where they catch more light. Scientists call this response phototropism. Growth can change again if the main source of light moves. The shoot does not turn by moving a joint in the way you turn an elbow.
facts: The same amount of light from different directions can change how a shoot bends.

questions.text: What do green leaves use the light for?
How does young sunflower stem growth help it change direction?
How do roots and stems respond to a different signal from their surroundings?

entries.title: Why do some ferns have dots under their leaves?
entries.answer: Turn over a mature leaf on some ferns and you may see rows of round brown spots. The spots are groups of tiny cases that hold spores. When spores are ready, those cases release them, and air can carry them away. In a suitable place, a spore can start a small separate stage of the fern’s life. Later a new leafy fern can grow. Ferns have roots, stems and leaves, yet they make no flowers or seeds.
facts: A fern leaf is also called a frond.

questions.text: Which smaller plants also spread through spores?
How does starting from a seed differ from growing from a spore?
What does the green surface of a fern frond do with sunlight?

entries.title: Why do some orchid flowers have surprising shapes?
entries.answer: Some orchid flowers have a broad part that gives an insect a place to land. Other parts can point into a space the visitor must pass through. An insect may brush against the flower and leave with a packet of pollen stuck to its body. When it visits a second flower of the same kind, the packet can touch the right surface. Different orchids use different shapes, smells or colors to attract visitors, and not every orchid depends on the same kind of animal.
facts: Some orchids stick a packet of pollen onto a visiting insect.

questions.text: What needs to happen to the pollen after it leaves a flower?
What familiar flavor comes from the fruit of an orchid?
What parts of a flower make it possible for pollen to leave and arrive?

entries.title: Why do some parts of a blue flag iris point up and others droop?
entries.answer: A northern blue flag iris often grows at the wet edge of a pond or marsh. When the flower opens, it has three smaller parts pointing upward and three broader parts that tip outward or downward. Some of the broader parts show white, yellow, or dark purple marks near their bases. Below the flower are long flat leaves shaped a bit like swords. They spread upward from the base in a tight fan.
facts: The plant also spreads from thick stems under the ground.

questions.text: Which other big flower can grow near a wetland?
How can an underground stem send up leaves in a new place?
What kinds of parts can show up around a flower's middle?

entries.title: Why do water drops roll off a lotus leaf?
entries.answer: A lotus leaf can look smooth from a distance. Up close, its surface has tiny bumps and a waxy coating. A drop of water touches only a small part of that surface, so it often rests as a round bead rather than spreading out like a puddle. As a drop rolls, it can pick up loose dirt. The shape of the leaf’s surface and the way water pulls on itself both help explain why a lotus leaf can stay cleaner after rain.
facts: A rolling drop can carry particles of dust away from a lotus leaf.

questions.text: Why does a little water drop tend to stay round?
What are some other jobs a leaf can do?
Where can the drops go after they leave the leaf?

entries.title: Why do western hemlock twigs look so fine and feathery?
entries.answer: Western hemlock twigs carry small, flat needles of different lengths. The mix gives the foliage a fine texture, especially at twig tips where you can see light between the needles. Farther down the branch, you may find little cones. Watch the highest point of a young tree from a distance. Instead of pointing stiffly at the sky, the tip can nod over to one side. Western hemlock can grow in shady forests along the Pacific side of North America.
facts: Western hemlock is Washington's state tree.

entries.title: Why does a bald cypress lose its needles in winter?
entries.answer: A bald cypress can look like an evergreen during summer. In autumn, its soft green leaves turn rusty and drop, so the branches look bare in winter. Even though it sheds its leaves, it still makes cones. Bald cypresses often grow in swamps and beside rivers. Sometimes you can see woody humps that rise above the water or soil near the trunk. These humps, called cypress knees, grow from the tree's roots.
facts: Bald cypress loses its needles even though it is a conifer.

entries.title: Why does a river birch look shaggy all year?
entries.answer: A young river birch trunk can look as though someone dressed it in curl after curl of thin brown paper. Some of the outer bark peels, but parts of the curls stay attached for a while. They often show several shades of tan, pink, or reddish brown. You may find the tree near streams or other moist ground. Even after its leaves fall, the bark can help you recognize it from far away.
facts: Older river birch trunks can develop darker, rougher bark.

entries.title: Why does a sycamore trunk look like a patchwork?
entries.answer: Look high on the trunk of an American sycamore. You may see light gray, tan, and creamy white patches on the same tree. Parts of its older outer bark flake away, showing smoother, lighter bark below. On many older trees, the bark near the bottom stays darker and rougher. You might also see round fruit balls on stalks. Some can hang from bare branches long after the leaves fall.
facts: The name buttonball tree comes from the round seed clusters.

entries.title: Why does a weeping willow look like a curtain?
entries.answer: Each of a weeping willow's long branches can have many thin side twigs that bend toward the ground. The twigs and their narrow leaves make a loose curtain below the crown. Some hang so low that they nearly touch the grass or water. Weeping willows are often seen near ponds, where the tips of the branches move in the breeze and their reflections can look like more branches growing down into the water.
facts: This kind of willow came from China.

entries.title: Why does a wild columbine flower have five long spurs?
entries.answer: An eastern red columbine has hanging red and yellow flowers. On the outside, five narrow tubes reach back from the petals like little fingers. Each tube, called a nectar spur, has nectar deep inside. A hummingbird can reach the nectar with its narrow bill and tongue. A visiting animal may brush against a flower's pollen-carrying parts while going after the sweet liquid. Columbines often open in spring along woodland edges or rocky places.
facts: The flowers usually hang downward from their stalks.

entries.title: Why does an aster flower look like a little purple sun?
entries.answer: Many New England asters have purple strips sticking out like sun rays around a yellow or orange middle. Up close, each flower head has many tiny flowers instead of just one. The purple parts help the plant stand out. The flowers in the middle can give visiting insects a place to land and feed. New England asters often bloom late, alongside other fall flowers in open, fairly moist places.
facts: New England asters are native to much of central and eastern North America.

entries.title: Why does an eastern hemlock cast deep shade?
entries.answer: An eastern hemlock has layers of branches with lots of small green needles. In a group of hemlocks, the branches can let very little sunlight reach the ground. Only certain plants grow well in that shade. Look closely at a twig and you may see needles that lie flatter than the pointed needles of many other cone-bearing trees. Small seed cones hang from the branches, often close to the twig tips.
facts: Young hemlocks can grow even where light is limited.

entries.title: Why does paper birch bark look like paper?
entries.answer: Long sheets curl out from the trunks of many older paper birches. Those thin sheets are part of the outer bark. They can look like scraps of white paper, while patches underneath may be orange or brown. Younger branches often have bark that looks darker and smoother. You can study the layers without pulling them off a tree. A loose piece on the ground can show the dark marks and the different colors on its two sides.
facts: Paper birch is also called canoe birch.

entries.title: Why does the air look snowy near a cottonwood in summer?
entries.answer: When seed pods on an eastern cottonwood open, fine white hairs can catch the breeze. Each tiny seed is carried along with some of those hairs. When a lot of seeds float away at once, the air may look full of white flakes. A seed has a better chance of starting when it lands on moist ground with plenty of light. Cottonwoods often grow beside rivers where floods can leave fresh, bare soil.
facts: Some cottonwoods produce seed pods, while others produce pollen.

entries.title: Why is a goldenrod branch covered with tiny yellow flowers?
entries.answer: What looks like one long yellow flower on Canada goldenrod is a branching spray of many small flower heads. An insect can walk or fly from one head to the next instead of hunting for each flower far away. Goldenrod often blooms late in the growing season. In an old field, its bright sprays can stand above the grasses when many earlier flowers have already gone to seed.
facts: Canada goldenrod can spread underground and come up as a group of stems.

entries.title: Why is a tomato a fruit?
entries.answer: In a tomato flower, a small part where seeds can develop, called the ovary grows into the tomato. That makes a tomato a fruit in botany, the study of plants. It has seeds inside, just as a peach or a grape does. A cucumber and a pea pod count as fruits for the same reason. People who cook often group these foods with vegetables because of how they taste and how we use them. Both groupings can be useful.
facts: Peas grow inside pods, which are fruits in botany.

entries.title: Why is a tuliptree named after a flower?
entries.answer: A tuliptree grows tall enough that flowers on its top branches can be hard to see from the ground. Look for cup-shaped blooms with greenish yellow and orange parts. They look a little like tulips, though they grow on a tree. The leaves are unusual too. The end of each wide leaf looks as if a small piece was clipped out, leaving a flat or dipped top instead of a single point.
facts: A tuliptree is a relative of magnolias.

entries.title: Why is a woodland flower named after a fish?
entries.answer: A yellow trout lily often has green leaves with uneven brown spots. The pattern can remind people of a trout's markings. A younger plant may make just one leaf and no flower. A flowering plant puts up two leaves and a bent stalk with a yellow bloom. It grows while spring light can reach the forest floor. Later its leaves die back, and much of the plant stays hidden underground until the next year.
facts: Some yellow trout lilies grow in large groups on the forest floor.

entries.title: Why is an American beech easy to spot in winter?
entries.answer: In a winter forest, an American beech may still have a few pale brown leaves on its branches. Many young beeches hold on to some dry leaves well after other trees are bare. Look at the trunk too. The bark usually stays smooth and gray even on a big tree. In the fall, a bristly fruit on a beech can open to show small, hard nuts that have three sides.
facts: American beeches can grow in some shade.

entries.title: Why is bamboo a grass when it looks like a tree?
entries.answer: Bamboo can grow tall, hard stems that look almost like small tree trunks. It is still in the grass family, along with lawn grass, wheat and rice. Many bamboo stems have hollow places between solid or stronger joints. A bamboo patch can put up shoots from stems that spread below ground. The hard stalks can be useful as building material in some designs. Their strength and size help explain why a big stand of bamboo can look more like woods than a lawn.
facts: Many bamboo stems have hard rings around places where leaves or branches grow.
